text:
maya: hey team — saw a sharp p99 token latency bump for /v1/chat/stream on Dedicated-03 right after the runtime change at 1798504000. checking KV cache stats now.
samir: which change? kernel selector tweak or batching heuristic? saw a small rollout earlier today.
maya: rollout was the kernel fallback ordering (prefer int8-kernel B before A for long-context models). suspecting suboptimal path for short prompts.
li-chen: i pulled perf traces — token-level breakdown shows decode time up ~30% and kv lookup time up ~4ms at p95. attaching snippet:
```
route=/v1/chat/stream
model=rwkv-14b
p50/token=3ms p95/token=8ms p99/token=22ms
kv_lookup_p99=7.8ms
kernel_exec_p99=12.1ms
```
henry: interesting — kv_lookup spike aligns with more evictions in prefix cache. eviction_count for Dedicated-03 jumped x4 after the change.
maya: where are we recording per-route reuse? perf-bot, can you post latest kv reuse by route?
perf-bot: kv_cache_summary: total_items=12430, total_memory=18.4GB, global_hit_rate=0.87, evictions=312 today. top routes by reuse: /embed=0.92, /v1/chat/stream=0.64, /rerank=0.78.
samir: /v1/chat/stream reuse 0.64 is low. Are we segregating prefix cache by model+route? iirc we shard by model and sequence bucket, not by route.
li-chen: yes — currently route isn't part of cache key, but route influences prompt prefixes heavily for our customers. different routes reuse prefixes poorly when mixed on same pool.
henry: suggests we add a lightweight route affinity tag to prefetch keys so hot prefixes for /v1/chat/stream stay colocated. small change in allocator.
maya: also saw more frequent kernel fallback to generic kernel A for short sequences. Samir, can you revert the ordering in a canary and check p99 token latency?
samir: can do a two-hour canary on Dedicated-03 with previous kernel order. will also enable detailed batching histogram export (per-batch-size token latency).
li-chen: if batching is producing bigger batches for this route because of changed timeout heuristic, that could increase queuing delay for first token. check batch size distribution.
perf-bot: current batch histogram for /v1/chat/stream (last 30m): size1=38%, size2=27%, size4=18%, size8=10%, >=16=7%.
maya: after the kernel tweak, size1 decreased by ~6% and >=16 increased by ~3% — suggests timeout threshold caused more waiting.
henry: timeline: rollout at 1798504000, latency spike observed at 1798504100, eviction ramp by 1798504200. looks like cascade: more batching -> longer KV retention pressure -> more evictions -> more kv_lookup cost.
samir: can reproduce locally with load generator: emulate mix of routes, change kernel fallback + batching timeout => p99 up. will revert kernel ordering and tighten batching timeout for canary.
li-chen: from instrumentation POV we should add per-route KV footprint and per-route eviction rate metric; current global metrics hide these hotspots.
maya: agreed. short-term: revert kernel ordering + decrease batching timeout on Dedicated-03. medium-term: per-route cache attribution, and a metric dashboard showing: kv_hit_rate_by_route, kv_evictions_by_route, kv_memory_by_route, batch_size_dist_by_route, token_latency_by_token_index.
henry: i can sketch dashboard panels. want: heatmap of token-level latency across token index and route, and stacked area for evictions-per-minute by route.
samir: deploying canary revert in 5m. will post logs. if p99 drops back we're good to rollback broadly.
maya: thanks. follow-ups: li-chen, add a short alert if kv_evictions_rate_for_route exceeds 1/s sustained for 2m. henry, add those panels to the runtime perf board.
li-chen: noted. i'll also add a trace tag for kernel-id to help correlate kernel selection with latency.
perf-bot: canary started at 1798504350 on Dedicated-03 with kernel-order=previous, batching_timeout=30ms.
samir: initial canary results after 60s: p99/token down from 22ms -> 15ms, kv_lookup_p99 down 7.8ms -> 3.1ms, eviction_rate down 4x -> 1.1x baseline.
maya: great — please keep canary for 15m then start gradual rollback. i'll update incident-postmortem if rollback goes full.
henry: will add dashboard tiles and a quick note in #all-hands ops update.
maya: closing loop — main action items: revert kernel order (samir), tighten batching timeout for latency-sensitive routes (samir), per-route kv metrics + eviction alert (li-chen), dashboard panels (henry). :thumbsup:
